question: What are the two most common first names among the school administrators? Indicate the district to which they administer.
clarification: Also keep rows that have no matching the joined table record.
gold: SELECT DISTINCT T1.AdmFName1, T1.District FROM schools AS T1 LEFT JOIN (SELECT admfname1 FROM schools GROUP BY admfname1 ORDER BY COUNT(admfname1) DESC LIMIT 2) AS T2 ON T1.AdmFName1 = T2.admfname1
gold0: SELECT DISTINCT T1.AdmFName1, T1.District FROM schools AS T1 INNER JOIN ( SELECT admfname1 FROM schools GROUP BY admfname1 ORDER BY COUNT(admfname1) DESC LIMIT 2 ) AS T2 ON T1.AdmFName1 = T2.admfname1

d.request: What are the two most common first names among school administrators, and which districts do they administer? Include rows even when there is no matching record in the joined table.
d.sql: WITH administrators AS (SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName1 AS first_name FROM schools WHERE AdmFName1 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(AdmFName1) <> '' UNION ALL SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName2 FROM schools WHERE AdmFName2 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(AdmFName2) <> '' UNION ALL SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName3 FROM schools WHERE AdmFName3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(AdmFName3) <> ''), top_names AS (SELECT first_name, COUNT(*) AS administrator_count FROM administrators GROUP BY first_name ORDER BY administrator_count DESC, first_name LIMIT 2) SELECT DISTINCT t.first_name, t.administrator_count, s.District AS district FROM top_names AS t LEFT JOIN administrators AS a ON a.first_name = t.first_name LEFT JOIN schools AS s ON s.CDSCode = a.CDSCode ORDER BY t.administrator_count DESC, t.first_name, district;

b.request: Find the two first names appearing most often across all three school administrator fields, list the districts of their schools, and retain schools even when a joined table has no matching record
b.sql: WITH administrator_names AS (SELECT s.District, CASE slot.n WHEN 1 THEN s.AdmFName1 WHEN 2 THEN s.AdmFName2 ELSE s.AdmFName3 END AS first_name FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode CROSS JOIN (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) AS slot), ranked_names AS (SELECT first_name, COUNT(*) AS appearances FROM administrator_names WHERE first_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(first_name) <> '' GROUP BY first_name ORDER BY appearances DESC, first_name LIMIT 2) SELECT r.first_name, r.appearances, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.District) AS districts FROM ranked_names AS r JOIN administrator_names AS a ON a.first_name = r.first_name GROUP BY r.first_name, r.appearances ORDER BY r.appearances DESC, r.first_name;

c.request:
What are the two most common first names among the school administrators? Indicate the district to which they administer.
Also keep rows that have no matching the joined table record.
c.sql: WITH administrators AS (SELECT CDSCode, TRIM(AdmFName1) AS first_name FROM schools UNION ALL SELECT CDSCode, TRIM(AdmFName2) FROM schools UNION ALL SELECT CDSCode, TRIM(AdmFName3) FROM schools), top_names AS (SELECT first_name, COUNT(*) AS administrator_count FROM administrators WHERE first_name IS NOT NULL AND first_name <> '' GROUP BY first_name ORDER BY administrator_count DESC, first_name LIMIT 2) SELECT DISTINCT t.first_name, t.administrator_count, s.District AS district FROM top_names AS t LEFT JOIN administrators AS a ON a.first_name = t.first_name LEFT JOIN schools AS s ON s.CDSCode = a.CDSCode ORDER BY t.administrator_count DESC, t.first_name, district;
